user.title: Grid Lens Setup
user.description: Tell us your location and create your GridLens account.

data_description.gridlens_email: Used to create your free GridLens account.

distributor.title: Select Your Network Distributor
distributor.description: Choose your electricity network distributor. Grid Lens currently has plan data for **Ausgrid** (Sydney, Central Coast, Newcastle, Hunter). Support for Endeavour Energy and Essential Energy is coming soon.

controlled_load.title: Controlled Load
controlled_load.description: Does your meter have a Controlled Load circuit switched by your network distributor? This is set by your DNSP based on your meter/wiring, not by your retail plan — check your switchboard or a past bill for a 'Controlled Load' line if unsure. Leave both off if you don't have one.

data_description.has_controlled_load_1: Tick if your meter has a Controlled Load 1 (CL1) circuit — commonly used for hot water or a pool pump, switched on by your network at set times.
data_description.has_controlled_load_2: Tick if your meter has a Controlled Load 2 (CL2) circuit, a second switched register some networks offer.

sensors.title: Energy Sensors
sensors.description:
{discovered}

Grid import and export sensors must measure cumulative energy (kWh/MWh) with state_class: total_increasing — not instantaneous power (W/kW).

data_description.energy_sensor: Cumulative kWh/MWh imported from the grid. Must have state_class: total_increasing.
data_description.solar_sensor: Cumulative kWh/MWh generated by your solar panels.
data_description.grid_export_sensor: Cumulative kWh/MWh exported to the grid.
data_description.grid_power_sensor: A live power sensor reading your home's net grid flow, in watts. Positive = importing from the grid, negative = exporting. Used by the Greedy Consumption feature to detect real export surplus. Optional.
data_description.import_price_sensor: Current import price in $/kWh from your retailer (e.g. sensor.flow_power_nsw1_import_price, sensor.amber_nsw1_general_price). Used to calculate your actual current-plan cost.
data_description.export_price_sensor: Current feed-in/export price in $/kWh from your retailer (e.g. sensor.flow_power_nsw1_export_price, sensor.amber_nsw1_feed_in_price).

battery.title: Battery Configuration
battery.description:
If you have a home battery, configure it here.

• Your current plan cost uses **actual** battery behaviour from your sensors.
• Alternative plans show costs with **optimally** scheduled battery usage so you can see the true potential saving.

data_description.battery_capacity: Total usable capacity in kWh (e.g. Sigenergy 10 kWh)
data_description.battery_min_soc: Reserve charge level to keep for backup (%)
data_description.battery_max_soc: Maximum charge level for battery health (%)
data_description.battery_soc_sensor: Sensor reporting current battery charge as a percentage (0–100).
data_description.battery_charge_power_sensor: Sensor for battery charging power. Use a signed sensor (positive = charging, negative = discharging) and leave Discharge blank — or supply two separate unipolar sensors (one for each direction).
data_description.battery_discharge_power_sensor: Discharge power sensor if separate from the charge sensor. Leave blank if your charge sensor is signed (negative when discharging).

inverter.title: Inverter / Battery Control
inverter.description:
{detected}

Grid Lens can actively manage your battery (charge/discharge) to follow the cheapest schedule. Select which inverter integration it should send commands to.

devices.title: Deferrable Loads
devices.description:
These appliances were found in your Energy Dashboard. Select any that can be **rescheduled to cheaper hours** — the optimizer will find the best time to run them under each plan.

Typical deferrable loads: EV charger, pool pump, dishwasher, washing machine, water heater.

device_power.title: Deferrable Load Power Limits
device_power.description:
For each device, enter its maximum rated power (kW) — this caps how much the optimizer can assign it in any hour.

Set each device's **allowed run times** afterward on the **Deferrable Loads** dashboard card (a paintable weekly schedule) — every device starts unrestricted (any hour) until you paint one.

Optionally pick a **control switch** for a device: a `switch.*` entity GridLens will turn on/off to run that load at the optimal times (each gets its own default-off master switch you enable when ready). Leave blank for forecast-only devices. Optionally pick a **battery/EV state of charge sensor** too — most relevant for an EV charger, shown on the Power Flow card like the home battery's SOC. Leave blank for loads with no battery of their own. If you told us earlier you have a Controlled Load circuit, you can also mark a device as wired to it — the register a device physically draws from, if any.

declared_loads.title: Declared (Unmonitored) Loads
declared_loads.description:
For a device with no HA-visible energy sensor at all — the normal case for a genuine Controlled Load circuit, which is wired separately from whatever an inverter's CT clamp monitors, so it usually can't be pointed at a sensor via the previous step — declare it here instead with an estimated **average daily kWh**. Up to 2 slots; leave the name blank to skip a slot.

If you told us earlier you have a Controlled Load circuit, you can mark a declared load as wired to it. Turn on **already counted in main reading** only if this load's energy is currently mixed into your main energy sensor (e.g. a general-circuit appliance you're considering moving to Controlled Load) — leave it off for a load already on a genuinely separate register (the normal case), since your main sensor never saw it in the first place.

data.in_aggregate_0: Load 1 — already counted in main reading
data.in_aggregate_1: Load 2 — already counted in main reading

current_plan.title: Your Current Plan
current_plan.description:
Select the electricity plan you are currently on.

This creates your **free Grid Lens account**, which compares your current plan against itself so you can see your cost breakdown.

[Upgrade at gridlens.au/pricing](https://gridlens.au/pricing) to compare against all available plans in your state and find out if you could be paying less.

data_description.has_demand_tariff: Tick this if your network bills a demand (peak kW) charge. It's set by your distributor based on your meter — check your bill for a 'demand' line in $/kW. When on, plans that include a demand charge have it added to the estimate, and the battery optimiser shaves your peak to reduce it.
data_description.vpp_program: If you're enrolled in a retailer VPP credit program on top of your plan (e.g. AGL Bring Your Own Battery), select it here. This is independent of your plan choice — switching plans with the same retailer won't affect it. Leave as 'None / not enrolled' if you're not in one.

subscribe.title: Unlock All Plans
subscribe.description:
Your free account compares your current plan only.

Subscribe to compare against every available plan in your state and find out if you're on the best deal. The next page will open gridlens.au — complete your subscription there, then return here automatically.

Or close that page to continue with your free account.

manual_key.title: Enter Your API Key
manual_key.description:
This Home Assistant installation is already registered with Grid Lens.

Enter your existing API key to compare against all available plans in your state.

Don't have a key yet? [Subscribe at gridlens.au/pricing](https://gridlens.au/pricing).

error.wrong_unit_power: This sensor measures power (W/kW), not energy. You need a cumulative energy sensor (kWh/MWh).
error.wrong_unit: Wrong unit of measurement — must be kWh or MWh.
error.wrong_state_class: This sensor does not have state_class: total_increasing. It may not be a cumulative energy sensor.
error.invalid_capacity: Battery capacity must be greater than 0 kWh.
error.invalid_hours: Invalid availability hours — use 'all' or ranges like '18-08' or '0-6,12-14'.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the GridLens API. Check the API URL and your internet connection.
error.invalid_api_key: Invalid API key — check the key and try again.
